title: Analyze
description:
`hpr analyze`: a flight log's readings, taken from the log alone, with no design file and no
simulation. Heights are meters above the pad, altitudes meters on the height track's own
scale (above the logger's zero for its own altitude); times are seconds on the log's clock.
Each reading states the bound its error stays within.

burnout.description: Burnout, from the axial accelerometer or the speed's peak.

drogue_descent.description: The descent under the drogue: from apogee to the main's opening.

flight_time.description: The flight time, liftoff to landing.

kind.description: What kind of result this is: every reading is measured, from the log.

landing.description: Landing, and the descent before it.

main_descent.description: The descent under the main, the canopy the rocket landed under.

max_acceleration.description: The top acceleration, from the axial accelerometer.

max_speed.description: The top vertical speed from liftoff to apogee.

stated.description:
What the file states about the flight: the logger's own figures, printed beside HPR Sim's
readings and never in place of them.

tool.title: Tool
tool.description:
The program that wrote a document or a file: the title block every `--json` document, every
file `hpr` writes and `hpr --version` carry (ADR-164; the product system's `data.md`: "Every
export carries the designation and version of the tool that made it").

designation.description: Its designation in the FusionSpace product system: `FS-ACHERNAR · SW · TOOL 001`.

trust.description:
The trust note the text form ends with: what the readings are, what they were checked
against, and what to go by instead (decision record ADR-213).

AccelerometerGravity.description: Whether an accelerometer's readings hold gravity.

oneOf.description: They hold it: the part reads +1 g standing on the pad.
They were written with it taken out: the part reads 0 on the pad.
A word this build of `hpr` doesn't name.

AnalyzeMethod.description:
How the readings were taken. `source` is `null` for a log with no height track, or one
withheld whole as `bad_record`; the other fields but `altitude_resolution_m` are `null` too
for a track too short to read, a GNSS track, or one withheld whole for its sampling or its
step, but for the interval or the step that withheld it; and `pad_altitude_m` for one
withheld as `no_climb`.

accelerometer.description:
The axial accelerometer the top acceleration and burnout came from; `null` when the log
has none, or none settled.

altitude_resolution_m.description: The altitude's resolution in the log's format, m: a PerfectFlite writes whole feet.

median_window_s.description: The running median's span, s: every height and time is read from the altitude after it.

pad_altitude_m.description:
The pad, on the track's own scale: the median of the track before it first rises 1 m,
m.

peak_bound_m.description: How far below its true peak the running median can read a peak bent by gravity alone, m.

sample_interval_s.description: The median interval between the track's samples, s.

source.description: The height track the readings were taken from.

step_m.description:
The track's step, m: the format's stated resolution, else the smallest gap between two of
its values; at the pad for a pressure track, whose step in height grows with height.

AnalyzedAccelerometer.description: The axial accelerometer the top acceleration and burnout came from.

column.description: The channel's column, as the file writes it.

gravity.description:
Whether its readings hold gravity's 1 g, or were written with it taken out; it is put
back for the readings.

sample_interval_s.description: The median interval between its samples, s.

turned_over.description: Whether its readings were turned over, as a part mounted nose down writes the thrust.

AnalyzedChannel.description: One column of the log `hpr analyze` read.

column.description: The column's name, as the file or the mapping writes it.

quantity.description: What it measures, which sets its unit: SI, but degrees for angles.

samples.description: How many samples it holds, gaps among them.

channels.description:
Every column the log holds, the primary track's among them, in the file's order:
`--record` prints their samples.

fip_header.description:
The FIP header file it was read under, as given (`--fip-header`); `null` for a log read
otherwise.

firmware.description: The logger's firmware version, as the file states it.

first_time_s.description: The primary track's first sample's time, s; 0 for a log that has none.

flight_number.description: The flight's number in the logger's memory, as the file states it.

last_time_s.description: The primary track's last sample's time, s; 0 for a log that has none.

layout.description:
The record layout file it was read by, as given (`--layout`); `null` for a log read
otherwise.

logger.description: The logger, as the file names it; `unknown` for a log read by a mapping or a layout.

mapping.description:
The column mapping file it was read by, as given (`--mapping`); `null` for a log read by
its format's own reader.

notes.description:
What the reader noticed and worked around, such as a sample count that differs from the
one the file states.

recording.description: The dump's recording chosen, from 0 (`--recording`); `null` for a file of one recording.

samples.description:
How many samples the primary track holds, the barometric altitude above the pad the
readings are taken from; 0 for a log that has none, such as a table read by a mapping
that marks none.

serial_number.description: The logger's serial number, as the file states it.

sheet.description:
The workbook's sheet chosen, from 0 (`--sheet`); `null` for a file that isn't a
workbook, or a workbook read with none chosen, whose one sheet that reads is read and
named in the log's first note.

altitude_m.description: The filtered track there, on its own scale, m.

bound_m.description:
The bound on the height's error, m: most of it the day's air, which moves a barometric
height by up to 6.9% of itself.

height_m.description: The height above the pad, m.

highest_sample.description:
The highest sample the track holds before the filter: above the apogee when the median
set a pulse aside.

is_floor.description: Whether the log may have ended before the peak, so the height is a floor.

time_after_liftoff_s.description: When, s after liftoff; `null` when liftoff is withheld.

time_bound_s.description: The bound on the time's error, s.

BurnoutReading.description: Burnout: when the motor stopped pushing.

bound_s.description: The bound on its error, s.

is_floor.description:
Whether the time is a floor: burnout came no sooner than it, less its bound, and may
have come later by any amount. A burnout from the speed's peak is.

provenance.description: Measured from the accelerometer; derived from the speed's peak.

source.description: The accelerometer, or the height track the speed came from.

time_after_liftoff_s.description: When, s after liftoff: the burn's length; `null` when liftoff is withheld.

time_s.description: When, s on the clock of the track it came from.

bound_m_s.description: The bound on its error, m/s.

from_height_m.description: The height at its start, m above the pad.

from_s.description: Where the leg starts, s: apogee, or the main's opening.

opening.description:
The main's opening, found back from landing, for the main's leg after a drogue's; `null`
for a drogue's leg or a descent under one canopy.

rate_m_s.description: The mean rate of descent over the leg, m/s, down positive.

to_height_m.description: The height at its end, m above the pad.

to_s.description: Where it ends, s: the main's opening, or landing.

FlightTimeReading.description: The flight time, liftoff to landing.

bound_s.description: The bound on its error, s: liftoff's and landing's.

GravitySettledBy.description: How an accelerometer's gravity was settled.

oneOf.description: By its family's word, which its pad and its coast agree with where they say.

By its pad, which reads near 1 g or near 0, where its family doesn't say; its coast, where
it says, agrees.

By its coast to apogee, which reads near 0 or near −1 g, where neither its family nor its
pad says.
A way this build of `hpr` doesn't name.

HighestSample.description: The highest sample of the track.

altitude_m.description: The track's value, on its own scale, m.

Kind.description: What kind of result a command printed: the kind every figure in it is.

oneOf.description: From a model of the flight, not measured.
Measured: an altimeter's log, or a weather balloon's sounding.
A weather model's forecast.
A reanalysis: a weather model's fit to past observations, such as ERA5.
Copied from a data file, such as a motor's curve file, or computed from it.

LandingReading.description: Landing, and the descent before it.

bound_s.description: The bound on its error, s.

mean_descent_rate_bound_m_s.description: The bound on the mean rate's error, m/s.

mean_descent_rate_m_s.description:
The mean rate of descent from apogee to landing, m/s: the height lost over the time
taken, drogue and main together.

time_s.description:
The first sample after apogee back within the pad's allowance that stays down for 1 s,
s: before touchdown by the time the last meters took.

bound_s.description: The bound on its error, s.

time_s.description: The last sample before apogee within the pad's allowance, s.

oneOf.description:
PerfectFlite's `.pf2`, as its software writes a Pnut's, a StratoLogger's or a
StratoLoggerCF's flights.

PerfectFlite's comma-separated export: a header row such as `Time, Altitude, Velocity,
Temperature (F), Voltage`, then rows in seconds and feet.

PerfectFlite's tab-separated text export: a header row such as `Time Altitude Temp.
Voltage`, then rows in seconds and feet.

AltOS's CSV, as AltosUI exports a TeleMetrum's, TeleMega's, EasyMega's or EasyMini's
flight: a `#version,serial,flight,…` header, then rows in SI.

The Featherweight Raven's FIP CSV, as the Featherweight Interface Program exports it: each
channel its own `Time@` column, its values, and a status column.

Missile Works' mDACS export of an RRC3's flight: a header row `Time, Altitude, Pressure,
Velocity, Temperature, Events, Voltages`, then rows on one clock.

An Eggtimer's flight data, as its own download writes it: a header row such as `T, Alt,
VRaw, VFilt`, then rows on one clock.

The Featherweight Blue Raven's CSV, as its phone app exports a flight: a low-rate file of
its barometric and inertial figures, or a high-rate file of its inertial sensors, each
with a header row such as `Year,Month,Day,Time,Flight_Time_(s),…`.

A Featherweight GPS tracker's CSV, as its ground station's app or software writes it: the
tracker's log, with a header row such as `UTCTIME,UNIXTIME,ALT,LAT,LON,#SATS,…`, or the
ground station's, such as `TRACKER,DATE,TIME,LAT,LON,ALT,…`. Positions only, no barometer.

A KML file (OGC 07-147r2) holding a GPS track as a path or a `gx:Track`, as AltOS, Missile
Works' RTx, Big Red Bee's BeeLine, fw2kml and others write it. Positions only.

A GPS receiver's NMEA 0183 sentences as it wrote them, such as `$GPGGA,…*hh`. Positions
only.

PerfectFlite's older `.pfa`, as its software saves an Alt15K/WD's flight: `Ground:`,
`Apogee:` and `NumSamps:` lines, then `**!!Data:` and one altitude a line.

An Eggtimer TRS's flight as its terminal download prints it: the flight settings and the
flight summary, then the table the CSV download writes.

AltimeterCloud's CSV of a Rocketry Ltd Nano V1's or Mercury's flight, as a flight page on
altimetercloud.com hands it back: a header row such as `Time(ms),Altitude(m),…`.

Entacore AIM's CSV, as its software exports a flight: each channel beside its own `time`
column.

AerospaceNU's SillyGoose flight computer's log, as the board writes it: tab-separated
text under a header such as `timestampMs pressurePa tempK …`.

Silicdyne's Fluctus flight computer's CSV: a `sep=;` line, then a semicolon-separated
table whose names carry their units, such as `time (ms);baro-altitude (m);…`.

Ozark Aerospace's ARTS2 interpreted data: a `# MET Acc Vel iAlt pAlt` header, then
comma-separated rows from launch.

AerospaceNU's flight computer board's CSV, as the club's tools write a flight: a header
row opening `,packetType,timestamp_ms,…` or `,timestamp_s,…`, then one row a sample.

AerospaceNU's ground station's text, as it parses the flight computer board's downlink: a
`RUN START` line, then one packet a line, `HH:MM:SS.ffffff: <packet> {…}`.

A phone app's `launch….csv`: a header row opening `Seconds,Timestamp,AltitudeMSLGPS,…`,
then one row a sample. The app isn't named in its files.

An Eggtimer TRS's terminal download, as [`LogFormat::EggtimerText`] reads it, saved inside
an RTF document.

The Featherweight Raven's raw download, `.FIPa`, as the Featherweight Interface Program
saves the altimeter's memory: a text header, then checksummed binary frames.

Missile Works' RRC3 raw flight file, `.rff`, as mDACS saves a download: a .NET
`BinaryFormatter` stream holding the altimeter's 16-bit words.

A Featherweight summary, as the Featherweight UI app exports a Blue Raven's or a GPS
tracker's flight beside its data: one `name,value` row a figure, such as `Max
Altitude,2500.25 feet`, and no samples.

AED Electronics' R-DAS raw data, as its Windows software exports a flight to text: a
`*** Configuration ***` section, then a table of the converters' counts.

AltOS radio telemetry, as AltosUI saves the packets a TeleDongle hears to a `.telem`
file: one `TELEM` line a packet, its bytes in hexadecimal.

AltOS's raw flight download, as AltosUI saves a flight computer's memory to an `.eeprom`
file: a JSON object of the board's configuration then the memory in hexadecimal, or, from
older versions, the configuration as the board prints it then one record a line.

Ozark Aerospace ARTS2's flight as its PC software saves it to an `.odf` file: the board's
settings and calibration, then the sensors' counts.

Ozark Aerospace ARTS2's raw data, as its PC software exports a flight: a
`MET,Acc(HI),Acc/Baro(LO),Baro(HI),State` header, then the sensors' counts.

Missile Works' RTx/GPS tracker's fixes, as mDACS saves a download to an `.rtx` file: a
.NET `BinaryFormatter` stream of one `List<Int32>`, each slot a 16-bit word mapped modulo
10⁹. Positions only.

The RTx's fixes as mDACS exports them to CSV: a `UTC Time,Latitude,Longitude,Altitude,…`
header, then one row a fix. Positions only.

The RTx's fixes as mDACS exports them to text: a tab-separated `UTC Lat Lon Alt …` header,
then one row a fix. Positions only.

A table of samples from a logger no other reader knows, read by what its header states: a
header row naming the columns, the units in the names, such as `Time (s),Alt AGL (ft)`,
then one row a sample ([`crate::generic`]); or read by a column mapping the caller gives.

A file of binary records end to end, each a run of fields, read by a layout the caller
states, since the file states none ([`crate::records`]).

A serial console's capture of a flight computer's shell, its memory dumped as base64
between marker lines such as `----++++//[[( data start )]]\\++++----`, each block's
records read by a layout the caller states ([`crate::capture`]).

The Featherweight Blue Raven's flight data as its USB port downloads it to a serial
terminal: one `@ LOG_LOW` or `@ LOG_HIR` line a sample, each closed by a CRC
([`crate::blueraven_usb`]).

A course's Teensy data logger, tab-separated: a sensor's tag, the clock in microseconds,
then its values, such as `Alt`, the clock, `P` and a pressure, `MSL` and an altitude
([`crate::teensy`]).

A course's Teensy data logger with named fields: units lines such as `MS5 data in us, deg
C, Pa`, then lines such as `MS5, t, 1330004120, T, 32.90, P, 92185` ([`crate::teensy`]).

One team's radio telemetry packets as text, one `255:…:254` packet a line, such as
`255:T:11:PP:100150:950.12:21.50:3.25:254`: the flight computer's own log, or what a
receiver heard ([`crate::packets`]).

The same packets in an RTF document a spreadsheet saved as CSV, one `255,…,254` packet a
line ([`crate::packets::read_rtf`]).

Rocketronics' AltiMAX, a flight as its PC software exports it to an `.xls` worksheet
([`crate::xls`]), read as a table headed `TIME,PRESS FILTER [hpa],HEIGHT FILTER [m],…`
([`crate::altimax`]).

A MARSA altimeter's flight download: its settings as `<NAME> value` lines, such as
`<BARO_ZERO 0> 790`, then a row a sample of the time, the altitude in feet and the
acceleration in g, such as `0.1,-29.0,8.65`; the `.dat` the altimeter's software saves, or
a spreadsheet's re-save of it ([`crate::marsa`]).

AltOS's radio telemetry decoded to a table, one row a packet under a header of the
packet's fields, `serial,tick,ptype,state,…,height,crc` ([`crate::altos_telem_csv`]).

Rocketronics' AltiMAX, a flight's `.ALS` file: a header, then a record of 22 bytes a
sample, its pressures, acceleration, event and one voltage channel's count
([`crate::altimax_als`]).

Entacore AIM XTRA, a flight as its software saves it to an `.xtra` file, a Boost binary
archive of one record a sensor group's sample ([`crate::entacore_raw`]).

Entacore AIM XTRA, one recording of its memory as its software downloads it, raw: a
type byte and big-endian fields a record, between bytes that count the clock's ticks
([`crate::entacore_raw::read_dump`]).

A GPX file, the GPS Exchange Format, version 1.0 or 1.1 as Topografix publishes it: its
tracks' points, each segment a GPS track ([`crate::gpx`]). Positions only.

LoggerStated.description: What a flight log states about the flight.

apogee_m.description:
The apogee the logger computed, m above its own zero; `null` if the file states none, or
states something that isn't a height, such as a PerfectFlite's `PWRLOSS`.

ground_elevation_msl_m.description: The launch site's elevation, m above mean sea level, as the logger states it.

MaxAccelerationReading.description: The top acceleration, from the axial accelerometer.

acceleration_m_s2.description:
The acceleration, m/s², along the rocket's axis as an accelerometer reads it: +1 g
standing on the pad, the thrust less the drag over the mass in the climb; less 9.81 m/s²,
the rocket's own acceleration up on a vertical climb.

bound_m_s2.description:
The bound on its error, m/s². When it is clipped, the true top is no lower than the
reading less the bound, and may be higher by any amount.

clip.description:
Why it is clipped: at the part's stated range, or held flat at its top below it or with
no range stated; `null` where it isn't.

is_floor.description:
Whether the top is a floor: no lower than the reading less its bound, and maybe higher by
any amount. A clipped top is, and so is one whose thrust the accelerometer shows no end to,
never falling through zero on the channel before apogee: that one is measured, its `clip`
`null`.

provenance.description: Clipped where `clip` says why; otherwise measured.

range_m_s2.description: The range of the part its family states, m/s²; `null` where it doesn't.

time_s.description: When, s on the accelerometer's clock.

MaxSpeedReading.description: The top vertical speed from liftoff to apogee, derived from the height track.

bound_m_s.description: The bound on its error, m/s.

height_m.description: The height above the pad then, m.

OpeningReading.description: The main's opening, found back from landing.

bound_s.description: The bound on its error, s.

height_m.description: The height then, m above the pad.

time_s.description: When, s: the first sample of the run back from landing whose rate stays near the main's.

Quantity.description:
What a channel measures. The unit is SI but for angles, which are in degrees as GNSS
receivers and loggers write them.

oneOf.description:
A barometric altitude above the logger's own zero, m; in a Featherweight GPS tracker's
summary ([`LogFormat::FeatherweightSummaryCsv`]), its receiver's altitude above the pad it
states.
A barometric altitude above mean sea level, m.
An altitude from GNSS, above mean sea level as the receiver states it, m.
An altitude the logger integrated from its accelerometer, above its zero, m.

An altitude whose sensor or zero the file doesn't state, m: a table read by its header
([`LogFormat::GenericTable`]) names an altitude and its unit, and often no more.
Air pressure, Pa.

A speed or velocity the logger computed, m/s; its column says from which sensor and along
which direction.
An acceleration, m/s²; its column says along which axis, and whether gravity is in it.
A temperature, K.
An electric potential, V, such as a battery's or a pyro channel's.
An electric current, A.
A latitude, degrees north.
A longitude, degrees east.
An angle, degrees, such as a tilt or a bearing.
A rate of turn, degrees per second, such as a gyroscope's about one of its axes.
A distance, m, such as a GNSS receiver's range from the pad.

A time of day on the logger's own clock, s after its midnight, in whatever time zone the
clock was set to: files state none.
A length of time, s, such as a summary's time from liftoff to an event.

A number with no unit, such as a count of satellites, a signal strength, a flag or a
state code, as the file writes it, or a fraction, such as a percentage the file writes,
divided by 100.

A column HPR Sim doesn't know: its values as the file writes them, in a unit HPR Sim
doesn't know either.

ReadingClip.description: Why a top acceleration is clipped.

oneOf.description:
It reaches the part's range as its family states it, within two steps and 0.25 g: the
part read no more.

It holds flat at its top, as a part that clipped holds it, short of any range the family
states or with none stated: the part may have clipped, at a range other than the one
stated.
A cause this build of `hpr` doesn't name.

ReadingMethod.description: How a reading was read off the track.

oneOf.description: The last sample before apogee within the pad's allowance.
The filtered track's highest value, at the middle of the run that holds it.
The steepest least-squares slope of the filtered track over 0.5 s.
The first sample after apogee back within the pad's allowance that stays down for 1 s.
The axial accelerometer's highest reading before apogee.

The first sample next to the axial accelerometer's least reading after it falls below
zero: the end of the thrust's fall.
The top speed's time, a floor: burnout came no sooner than it less its bound.
Landing's time less liftoff's.
The height a leg of the descent loses over the time it takes.
A method this build of `hpr` doesn't name.

ReadingProvenance.description: Whether a reading was measured on the track, derived from it, or clipped by it.

oneOf.description: A time or height read off the filtered track.
Worked out from the track, such as a speed from its slope.
Measured, but at the sensor's range, so the true value may lie beyond it.
A provenance this build of `hpr` doesn't name.

ReadingSource.description: The height track a reading came from.

oneOf.description: The logger's own barometric altitude, the record's primary track.
A pressure channel, turned into a height by the 1976 standard atmosphere.
A barometric altitude kept in a channel, above the pad or above sea level.
A GNSS receiver's altitude: no reading is taken from it.
The accelerometer along the rocket's axis.
A source this build of `hpr` doesn't name.

detail.description: The reason in words, with the log's own numbers.

WithheldReason.description: The reason a reading was withheld.

oneOf.description: The height track has fewer than three samples.

The track never climbs 3 m above the pad, or the liftoff allowance and a step if that is
higher; or, for landing, falls too little past its step and noise to time the descent.

A track whose heights are above the pad only by a mapping's or a column's word starts
more than 19.9 m from its zero, more than the weather and the noise move a zero in an hour
on the pad: the log didn't start on the pad, or its heights aren't above the pad, as an
altitude above sea level mapped as one above the ground reads.
The log ends before the rocket is seen to land.
The track reaches the ground sooner than a fall from rest at apogee in vacuum could.
The top speed is above 4,000 m/s.
The climb's speed swings negative by more than 20% of its top.
The log has no accelerometer.
The reading needs another, which was withheld.
The record breaks what every reader guarantees; only a record built by hand can.
The samples come more often than 500 a second, faster than the bounds were checked at.
The log holds no altitude, pressure or GNSS track.
The log's only height doesn't say whether a barometer or a GNSS receiver measured it.

The track is sampled more slowly than the readings were checked at, 2 s between samples,
or, for the top speed, too slowly for its fit.
The track moves in steps coarser than the readings were checked at: 10 m, or 100 Pa.

The climb reaches Mach 0.8 in the coldest air the bounds allow, where the barometer's port
may read the transonic flow over the nose.
The only height is a GNSS receiver's, whose filter lags a climb and overshoots its top.
The only height is a GNSS receiver's, whose fix drops out or lags at liftoff.

The track loses no more than its noise and step in the 4 s before its top: its clock is
in another unit, such as milliseconds read as seconds, its top isn't a coast's, or it
isn't a height.

The log's first samples can't rule out a rocket already more than 2 m up when it starts:
it starts after liftoff, as a logger that records from launch writes its zero and then the
climb, or holds too little of the pad to tell liftoff by. A track above the logger's own
zero, or one a mapping or a header calls above the ground, still gives its heights from
that zero, with the zero's possible error in their bounds.
The height track's clock doesn't increase, so no time can be read off it.

The track falls past its noise and step below a peak in the 4 s before its top, then
climbs to it: a coast doesn't, and a disturbance after apogee, such as a deployment's, does,
so which is the apogee can't be told.

The log's accelerometers don't say which lies along the rocket's axis, such as a board's
three axes: the top acceleration and a burnout from the accelerometer need the axial one.

The axial accelerometer's readings may or may not hold gravity's 1 g, and none of its
family, its pad and its coast to apogee settles which, or they disagree.

Which way up the axial accelerometer reads isn't settled, or it shows no thrust. Of its
three witnesses, each on the trace as written, none says or two disagree: the pad (about
1 g nose up, about −1 g nose down), the coast to apogee (−0.75 g or less nose up, 0.75 g
or more nose down) and the thrust (its first span past 2 g to hold there for 0.5 s,
unless a span the other way comes first). Or, turned as they settle and gravity put back,
it never reads past 2 g from liftoff's earliest time to apogee.
